title: The Crazy Blues record craze at the store
summary: Mamie Smith's record started a rush; customers lined up around the block for new Bessie and Mamie Smith records priced from sixty-five cents to a dollar.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: Mamie Smith came out with 'Crazy Blues.' That started them, you know. And then we couldn't get enough records, you know, for a year or two. We'd get in fifty or a hundred records, and they'd be gone in an hour. 'Cause we'd put a just sign up on the door out in front: 'Bessie Smith New Record In' or 'Mamie Smith New Record In' and...and in two...three hours, people be standing in line half a block waiting to get...get up there to get a record. That's when they first come in, you know. That lasted maybe three or four months, then everybody...it slowed down, and they'd come in and get records all along, you know, but when they first come out, oh, my God, they would just stand in line for a block, waiting for her, to get the records.
How much did the records sell for then?
